paper_metadata.title: A Quantum Algorithm for Pricing Asian Options on Valuation Trees

summary: The paper proposes a gate‑based quantum circuit for pricing discrete floating‑strike Asian options using valuation trees and amplitude‑encoded payoffs. Simulator experiments on a binomial model with up to 5 time steps use 13–23 qubits and 67–1229 CNOT gates, with results obtained from up to 10^7 shots per configuration; the claimed quadratic speedup comes only from theoretical compatibility with amplitude estimation and is not experimentally demonstrated.

experiments.description: Quantum circuit simulation of a valuation-tree-based discrete floating-strike Asian option pricing algorithm on a binomial model, evaluated for different time-step counts and positive-part approximation settings.

algorithm.variant: Amplitude-based valuation-tree Asian option pricing with gearbox-style positive-part approximation; compatible with amplitude estimation

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Paths through the valuation tree are encoded in an N-qubit state register; for the binomial model used in results, one qubit per time step encodes up/down decisions. Path probabilities are loaded into amplitudes; payoff and positive-part indicator are encoded via additional ancilla qubits and amplitude arithmetic.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Positive part implemented approximately via gearbox circuit; amplitude subtraction and controlled operations used to combine payoff terms; no explicit optimization constraints.

problem_instance.description: Discrete floating-strike Asian option pricing on a valuation tree using a Rendleman-Bartter binomial model with equal up/down probabilities.

dataset_specification.description: Underlying starts at S(0)=1; risk-neutral evolution with u=exp((r-sigma^2/2)Δt + sigma sqrt(Δt)), d=exp((r-sigma^2/2)Δt - sigma sqrt(Δt)); r=0, sigma=0.2, T=1.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Classical precomputation of underlying values on the valuation tree; normalization by M=max_{t_i,k} S_k(t_i) for amplitude encoding.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Simulated on Qiskit simulator; for individual path evaluation, 10^7 shots; for full pricing histograms, 10^6 circuit executions per data point and 100 data points per parameter setting.

implementation_details.classical_solver: classical valuation-tree precomputation; Monte Carlo/classical binomial-tree comparison for exact reference
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Compute valuation-tree node values and normalize underlying values; construct Fourier-series approximation and gearbox parameters; for the binomial model, map each path to a bitstring of up/down decisions.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Rescale measured probabilities to recover option price; compare against analytical/classical binomial-tree values; compute absolute errors and histograms.

speedup_claims.conditions: if quantum amplitude estimation is used with a properly constructed amplitude encoding; fault-tolerant or sufficiently deep hardware assumed
speedup_claims.caveats: The reported experiments were run on a simulator and did not use amplitude estimation due to circuit depth restrictions.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(1/Ns) amplitude-estimation convergence for probability estimation; circuit resources scale with valuation-tree size and state-preparation cost, with uniformly controlled rotations requiring O(2^n) CNOTs in the presented implementation.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Requires scalable fault‑tolerant quantum hardware capable of running amplitude estimation circuits for valuation-tree option pricing with deep uniformly controlled rotations; current experiments only simulate circuits up to ~23 qubits and ≤1229 CNOTs.
limiting_factors: Experiments performed only on noiseless simulator
Amplitude estimation not actually executed due to circuit depth limits
Uniformly controlled rotations scale O(2^n) in CNOT gates
State preparation overhead for probability distributions
Problem sizes limited to ≤6 time steps in resource analysis

notes: hardware.type inferred as simulator_other because the paper states evaluations were performed with a quantum computer simulator and names Qiskit simulator, not a real QPU.
num_qubits reported from Table 1 and the text: width equals 13/15/16/18/19 for D=1,n_f=4 and 17/19/20/22/23 for D=2 settings; the paper also states one qubit per time step plus ancillas.
circuit_depth not explicitly reported; only CNOT counts and width are given, so depth is left null.
The paper claims quadratic speed-up via amplitude estimation, but the actual experiments are simulator-based and do not run AE due to depth restrictions.

The paper discusses a theoretical quadratic speed-up via amplitude estimation (Section 4.6) but explicitly states the experiments are simulator-based and AE was not used due to circuit depth restrictions.
All reported results are demonstrations on a quantum simulator for small toy binomial trees rather than performance comparisons with classical algorithms.
